accuracy.evidence: Every pairing was checked against standard young-animal names: sheep/lamb, cow/calf, cat/kitten, duck/duckling, dog/puppy, pig/piglet, horse/foal, and chick as the young of the chicken with the hen as its mother. A first draft said 'a chick is a baby hen'; that was corrected to 'a baby chicken' (half of chicks grow into roosters), the sorter bin now asks whose baby it is rather than what it grows into, and the name step uses a sheep instead of a hen. Matches the topic's evidence statements: names the babies, matches grown-ups with babies, says a kitten grows into a cat.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips of two- and three-year-olds and the ones named in the adult text: one baby word for every animal (name step offers kitten and calf for a dog; challenge 'A puppy' for a baby cat), chick and duckling mixed up (challenge tags bird and bird2, m4 'A hen'), babies staying small ('It stays a puppy', 'A bigger duckling', p3 'A bigger calf for ever'), growing into a different animal (grow step offers a dog for the kitten and a duck for the chick), and big/small confusion ('The big sheep', 'They are both babies').

lab_distinct.evidence: Every mechanic is about parent and young: a baby card is dragged to one of three grown-ups, a grown-up's baby name is chosen from names of other babies, a kitten and chick grow in two taps and then must be named as the right grown-up, six animals are sorted by being a baby or a grown-up with babies drawn as small copies of the adult, and a farm page asks for a baby and then its own mother. The distinctness gate passed against every flagship lab, including flagsense and flagfeel for this age.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the idea by acting: taking the lamb to the cow answers 'That is a cow. A cow's baby is a calf. Look for a big sheep'; tapping the big sheep when asked for the lamb says 'A baby is small'; the kitten visibly gets bigger, and choosing 'a dog' says it grows into a cat like its mummy. Each finished task names the rule: a baby is a small one of the same animal; babies are small, grown-ups are big; lamb and sheep, chick and hen, calf and cow.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'A lamb is a baby. Who is its mummy? A cow / A sheep' (the cow is the first grown-up shown and tapping it is corrected), 'What do we call a baby dog? A kitten / A puppy' (kitten is offered and named as a baby cat), and 'The kitten grows and grows. What will it be? A dog / A cat' (the grown kitten has 'a dog' as a choice that is corrected).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with rotated answer order and a streak count; twelve wrong-answer messages each name the slip, e.g. 'A cat's baby is a kitten. A calf is a baby cow', 'Babies do not stay small. A puppy grows into a dog', 'The big one is the grown-up. The baby is the small one', 'Ducklings grow into ducks, not hens. Chicks grow into chickens', 'A puppy is a baby dog. A baby cat is a kitten'.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses only short sentences of two-to-eight everyday words ('A lamb is a baby sheep.'), passing the family kid limit in validate_lessons; adult text passes the adult limit. In the lab every screen carries one short line ('Who is the lamb's mummy?', 'Tap the lamb.') with large animal pictures and a word under each, so an adult can read it aloud to a pre-reader.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs each carry one idea: babies are small and mummies big, four baby names, four more names, babies grow into their own kind. Adult paragraphs give what the topic is for, what each lab step does, four named mistakes with a fix (say both words together), and a toy-animal question game. The sorter (whose baby is it: sheep, cow or hen) is not a copy of any lab step.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 dark and 360 px Android light screenshots of all six steps. Fixed one problem seen in the first shots: emoji were drawn with the card's translucent fill and looked faded, so the animal pictures now draw at full strength, and the baby in the top card was enlarged. Tap targets are cards about a third of the canvas wide and over 100 px tall plus full-width button twins; nothing is clipped at 360 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: a labelled button per grown-up ('Take the baby to the sheep'), a button per baby name, 'Grow a bit' and the three grown-up choices, Baby and Grown-up buttons for sorting, and a labelled button for each of the six farm-page pictures ('Tap the lamb'). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action, e.g. 'Baby: lamb. Grown-ups: cow, sheep, duck.' Challenge feedback is a polite live region with a text tick or cross; the walkthrough's axe run (WCAG 2.1 AA) was clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
